reason: E1 shows that thermal exposure of a similar HEA coating at 800 °C forms Cr2O3 and spinel oxides and enhances wear resistance, supporting the first two premises. However, E1 does not involve pre-oxidation under load, so the claim that pre-oxidation under load produces a stable, adherent layer is not directly supported. E2 and E3 are about different alloys (AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5) or different conditions (room temperature, vacuum heat treatment), providing no specific evidence for the key premises about FeNiCrCoCu at 800 °C.
premises: FeNiCrCoCu coating forms Cr2O3 and spinel oxides upon thermal exposure at 800 °C
Such oxide layers enhance wear resistance
Pre-oxidation at 800 °C under load will produce a stable, adherent oxide layer
The oxide layer acts as a mechanical barrier and lubricious film reducing wear
The oxide layer maintains microhardness and resists surface degradation at high temperature
